The most general form pro- posed by Hill replaces the exponent 4 with a number n that is chosen to fit particular situations. n  1 corre- sponds to the myoglobin case with no cooperativity, and a fit to the hemoglobin curve produces n  2.8, which demonstrates a high degree of, but not perfect, cooperativity.

The four equilibrium constants are not equal to each other, and K4 is much larger than the other three. Re- ducing PO2 clearly reduces the fraction of bound oxygen (Le Châtelier’s principle) for both proteins but the two molecules respond quite differently to decreasing oxy- gen partial pressures.
